P1.evidence: Clean on all four despite a mid-pipeline handoff the rep had to declare up front — 'By the way, I'm taking over for Andrew, so my name's Michael, just as a heads up.' Application read back: 'I went through everything, plus your application, so I have a decent head start on where we're at with things.' Full four-part frame delivered: 'where you're at today, where you want to go, what's been getting in the way, and what you genuinely need to get there.' Agreement taken: 'That all sound good? Yeah.' Open question asked: 'Walk me through what could we potentially help you with today? Give me an overview.'

P2.evidence: The most complete baseline in the batch and the rep signposted it — 'I want to get some baseline here before we dive in deeper.' Age confirmed, height and weight asked directly (5'10", 174). Work covered thoroughly including physical demand: 32 years as a UPS delivery driver walking five to ten miles a day. Injuries asked directly and followed properly — 'anything else like injury-wise, chronic pain, anything that limits movement?' and then 'Did you have surgery on it?' — surfacing the Achilles repair, the shattered radius and the meniscus. Training week, results ('What have you noticed?'), diet, sleep with a cause probe, and energy all asked and answered. P2c is partial on two counts: hereditary conditions were never asked, and although the rep did ask 'What about any chronic health conditions, anything health condition-wise?', he asked nothing at all after being told about AFib and SVT with surgical repair. The gathering was excellent; nothing was done with what was gathered.

P3.evidence: Front half ran, back half did not. P3a: 'how are we feeling about the physique currently?' produced the core and lower-back answer. P3b asked explicitly: 'what about like mobility, um, energy, different things like that?' P3d was asked well — 'what's the motivation? What's those things, man? Like, why is athleticism important? Why is the longevity stuff important?' — and produced the strongest material on the call, the painful last years at UPS and the wish to redirect that energy inward. Then it stopped. P3c was never asked, which is a real loss given he had a meniscus injury that stopped him descending a mountain a year ago. No future-pace exercise of any kind was run, so P3e is a miss. P3f was never asked and the rep never established whether this man has children or anyone depending on him — after 54 minutes we know he is divorced and lives alone and nothing more. P3g reached longevity and touched identity ('I've always been a fairly good athlete, considered myself one') but nothing on family or legacy. No reflect-back at any point.

P4.evidence: Effectively skipped, and this is the strategic failure of the call. 'What have you tried before?', 'What happened with that?' and 'Why do you feel it didn't stick?' were all never asked. P4d and P4e get partial credit for one good question — 'what's having us want to push to the next level now, of a sudden, given you've had kind of an entire year?' — which did surface travel as the structural barrier. P4f is the glaring one. This prospect had just told the rep he has trained consistently for 17 straight weeks, walks 137 miles a month, and self-rehabilitated a meniscus injury well enough to hike three 4,000-footers. He is living proof that he can stick to things on his own, and he even said so — 'And I have done that the last 17 weeks.' The script's job here is to establish that the information is not the problem and structure is; instead the rep left the prospect's strongest reason not to buy completely unexamined. When the price landed there was no established gap for it to fill.

P5.evidence: No consequence frame. The two-year question was never asked in any form, he was never asked whether he would settle for that, and 'why not?' never came. P5d gets partial only because the rep used the phrase, but as a leading summary rather than a commitment: 'it's seeming like now is kind of the time to draw a line in the sand and really get in, like, really put your head down and get the work in. Is that what I'm understanding?' The prospect half-rejected it — 'Yeah. And I have done that the last 17 weeks' — which is a correction, not agreement, and the rep took it as a yes and moved on. The material for a devastating P5 was sitting on the table: a 63-year-old with residual AFib, a repaired Achilles, a meniscus history and a stated fear of a devastating injury, whose whole retirement plan depends on his body holding up for twenty more years. None of it was used. This is the second consecutive call in this batch where P5 simply did not run.

P6.evidence: Both questions asked, and the rep deserves credit for pushing on the soft answer. P6a: 'Having all that dialed in, that everything that you need to actually become that, you know, 70, 80-year-old surfer... Do you feel like that's everything you need?' got a soft 'I would hope so, yeah', and the rep correctly pressed — 'Anything you think might be missing? Anything at all. Be honest with us.' P6b: 'if we can figure out all the details, you're fully committed to showing up, doing the work, following the program, asking questions when you need it, like you're fully committed to that?' P6c is a clear miss and it decided the call. The answer was not a yes: 'Oh yeah. I mean, if, yeah, if the price is right, sure. You know? I'm on a fixed income now.' That is a conditional plus a volunteered financial constraint, which the script says to treat as hesitation and return to Phase 5. There was no Phase 5 to return to, and the rep quoted $6,000 in the very next breath.

P11.evidence: A close was attempted — 'if we could break it up, is that something you'd want to hop on, like, hey, let's rock and roll right now?' — so the phase applies. No payment was collected and the prospect declined explicitly. Steps two to four were unreachable. Worth noting as a separate weakness: having failed on payment, the rep did not fall back to anything concrete. No deposit, no held calendar slot, no firm payment-plan figure to consider, not even a booked follow-up call — just 'I'll shoot you a text' on a prospect who had said he would have an answer in 24 hours.

objection_plays.detail: The best-run money play in the batch, and it still stalled halfway. What ran, and ran well: the isolation — 'just quadruple checking, like finances aside, like it does kind of check all the boxes for you... Correct?' answered 'Oh yeah. That's not the issue.' The should-versus-how reframe, almost verbatim from the script — 'it sounds like we're really not in a place where it's like, should I be doing this?... It's more of a matter of like, how can I actually make this work at this point?' answered 'Yeah. I would absolutely love to do it. But I just got to figure out how now.' The break-it-up offer — 'most people do pay for it upfront... do you want to just have an open conversation about where we're at financially? Maybe we can figure out a way to make it work right now.' And the permission question, answered 'Sure. Yeah, fair enough.' Two of the six financial-picture questions ran: cash on hand ('Where are we actually sitting at cash-wise right now? Like what do we actually have available checking savings?') and monthly surplus ('after you've kind of covered your expenses each month, like how much is typically left over month to month to play around with?'). Both got deflections — 'I've got money to cover everything' and 'I really don't look at it that way' — and the rep accepted both without a second attempt, so no actual number was ever obtained. Nothing on credit cards, available credit, used versus available, or investments; the 401k surfaced only incidentally through the friend who manages it. The play then died in rapport: the rep followed the prospect into Sardinia, a lost surfboard in Bogotá and what it feels like to drop into a wave, and never came back to the numbers.

Triggered twice and never played. 'I would have to take some time and think about that one' at 00:40:59, then hardened at 00:53:08 into 'I still need that 24 hour period to think about this... I can't commit verbally right now.' Not one OA move ran. No 'do you feel what we've gone through CAN get you to your goal?' as a standalone (the equivalent question ran inside OC, which is the only overlap). No 'thinking isn't the problem, deciding is.' No 'the way you've been approaching this brought you here — when do you make a different decision?' No 'so what's actually coming up that's preventing you from getting started?' The rep's entire response to a stated intention to deliberate was 'Okay. Yeah. Not an issue', and later a text arrangement.

Present in substance and unrecognised. 'It's just a matter of whether it's the right fit for me at this point in my life', plus a year of postponement already attributed to travel, plus four and a half months on the road in the last twelve, plus provisional trips he will not know about for three weeks. That is the not-the-right-time objection wearing a calendar. None of the play ran. The scripted line that fits this prospect better than any other in the playbook — 'the longer you wait the harder this gets, metabolism slows, injuries compound' — was available to use on a 63-year-old with a repaired Achilles, a meniscus history and residual AFib, and was never said. 'Things never slow down' and 'when does it actually become the right time?' were also never said, on a retiree whose travel schedule is now permanent.

Script gap worth recording. The prospect's real barrier to the product is that he travels four and a half months a year and cannot take kettlebells with him — 'you can't carry kettlebells with you... it's difficult to work out and keep a set routine. So that's delayed my decision a little bit.' The playbook has no play, and no product answer, for a prospect whose life makes the equipment intermittently unavailable. The rep addressed travel once, on nutrition, and never on training. A prospect can be perfectly qualified, perfectly willing and still structurally unable to use the programme half the year, and nothing in the process is designed to surface or solve that.

notes: Best baseline and best money play of the batch sitting on top of no P4 and no P5. The rep gathered an outstanding picture of this man and then built nothing with it: the prospect's 17 unbroken weeks of self-directed training were never confronted as a reason not to buy, and a 63-year-old with a cardiac history and three surgical repairs was never shown a cost of waiting. Two specific coaching actions. Run P4f whenever the prospect is already succeeding alone, because that is exactly when the structure argument has to be made explicitly. And when a financial-picture question gets a non-answer like 'I really don't look at it that way', ask again — both deflections were accepted first time and the play collapsed into travel talk immediately afterwards.
